summary.text: Bruce Whalley is the One Nation candidate for Bundoora at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC, he set up a communications consultancy and, once retired from it, took up driving Melbourne trams, where he became known for his rapport with passengers. He has been one of the regulars on the ABC quiz program Think Tank, whose Wikipedia entry notes his tram-driver nickname. One Nation's page for him refused our requests, so it is not used here.

sources.title: Bundoora: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Think Tank (Australian game show), Wikipedia

summary.text: Chloe Nicolosi is the Animal Justice Party's candidate for Bundoora at the 2026 Victorian election. She works as a corporate analyst in emerging technologies, is studying for a Juris Doctor, and was named Zoos Victoria's Young Advocate of the Year in 2013. In mid-2026 the party presented her as its North-Eastern Metropolitan Region upper-house candidate, and Wikipedia still lists her there, but by November the party's pages named her only for Bundoora.

occupation.text: Corporate analyst working with emerging technologies

prior_roles.note: The party page says she has had this experience but gives no years or organisation.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Chloe Nicolosi as the Animal Justice candidate for McEwen; same name and party, but no source links that candidacy to her directly.

priorities.text: End live animal exports
Phase out factory farming, for animal welfare and to cut emissions
Public investment in cultivated meat and precision fermentation
More affordable housing, including limits on negative gearing
End 1080 baiting and recreational hunting to protect native wildlife

summary.text: Chris Parr is standing for the Liberals in Bundoora at the 2026 Victorian election. Born and brought up in Bundoora, he began his career in retail management and then set up his own landscaping business, which the ABC says he has run for 13 years. He stood for the Liberals in the federal seat of Jagajaga in 2025, which Labor held.

priorities.text: Reducing crime
Lower living costs for local families
A state government that works

summary.text: Colin Brooks has represented Bundoora for Labor since 2006. He was Speaker of the Legislative Assembly from 2017 to 2022, then joined the ministry, and has been Treasurer and Minister for Industrial Relations since August 2026. He is recontesting Bundoora in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Minister for Industry and Advanced Manufacturing
prior_roles.note: Parliament gives the start as December 2024; Wikipedia gives October 2023.

Minister for Child Protection and Family Services
Minister for Disability, Ageing and Carers

prior_roles.note: Wikipedia gives the start year only.

priorities.text: Keeping people healthy and safe
Access to good jobs and a sound education
Upgrades to public transport and roads
More jobs in renewable energy to address climate change
Education from kindergarten through to TAFE and university

summary.text: Melissa Murphy-Webster is standing as an independent for Bundoora at the 2026 Victorian election. Her career has been in retail and food production: she spent seven years running loss prevention for Chemist Warehouse and now directs a business that makes vegan cheese. She has an MBA from Swinburne University, and in 2024 she ran unsuccessfully as an independent in Banyule City Council's Ibbott Ward.

occupation.text: Director of a vegan cheese manufacturer

priorities.text: I will oppose any new taxes or tax increases.
Cutting red tape and regulation that weigh on small businesses
Upgrading Watsonia station at the same time as any new car park there
Lasting limits on trucks using local roads in the north-east once North East Link opens
Clearer legal protection for people who defend themselves inside their own home

summary.text: Nina Laitala is the Greens candidate for Bundoora at the 2026 Victorian election. Her current work is training boards and volunteers in governance and leadership across Australia, and for seven years she was chief executive of the Victorian Student Representative Council. She says she has three teenage children and comes from a migrant family, and she has also developed community music and arts projects.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's results list a Greens candidate named Nina Laitala; same name and party, but no source we read says it was her.

priorities.text: Making life more affordable for Bundoora households
Listening to the community and acting with integrity
Wider access to the arts and culture, especially for young people

summary.text: Rae Rancie is the Family First candidate for Bundoora at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Her party page describes her as a long-time Nillumbik resident and former small business owner with 10 children and 28 grandchildren, who spent three years in China with her husband teaching and doing humanitarian work. A candidate of the same name stood in Wingrove Ward of Nillumbik Shire in 2024 and for Family First in Jagajaga at the 2025 federal election.

prior_roles.role: Teaching and humanitarian aid work in China (three years)

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Rae Rancie (Independent) in this ward. No source says this is the 2026 Bundoora candidate, though the name is uncommon and her party page says she lives in Nillumbik.
Wikipedia lists a Rae Rancie as the Family First candidate. No source says this is the 2026 Bundoora candidate, though the name is uncommon and her party page says she lives in Nillumbik.

priorities.text: Support for families and local businesses, and more chances for young people to thrive
Practical, common-sense solutions that bring the community together
Keeping the Western and Judeo-Christian foundations of Australian life

summary.text: Sagar Sanyal is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Bundoora at the 2026 Victorian election. He says he has lived in Melbourne's outer north-east for many years and has been at home raising young children; his earlier jobs include school reception, factory work and a job in tertiary education. He has belonged to the National Tertiary Education Union and the Australian Manufacturing Workers' Union, and has campaigned on public housing, climate change and Palestine.

priorities.text: I want a society that puts people before profits.
Opposing policies that favour developers and corporations over working people
Better public health, education, welfare and housing
Opposing blame of migrants for the housing crisis and wider police powers
